facts.statement: Elosuchus possessed an elongated snout similar to a gharial and was likely a fully aquatic animal.
facts.quote: Elosuchus had an elongated snout like a gharial and was probably a fully aquatic animal.

facts.statement: The type species E. cherifiensis was originally described as a species of Thoracosaurus by Lavocat but was recognized as a separate genus by de Broin in 2002.
facts.quote: The type species, E. cherifiensis from Algeria and Morocco, was originally described as a species of Thoracosaurus by Lavocat, but was recognized as a genus separate from Thoracosaurus by de Broin in 2002.

facts.statement: A large skull measuring approximately 1.08 meters long indicates that the animal could reach a body length of up to 7.7 meters.
facts.quote: The large skull measuring approximately 1.08 m long indicates a body length of up to 7.7 m.

facts.statement: De Broin created the family Elosuchidae in 2002 to contain Elosuchus and the genus Stolokrosuchus from Niger.
facts.quote: de Broin (2002) created the family Elosuchidae to contain Elosuchus and the genus Stolokrosuchus from Niger.

facts.statement: There is debate regarding Elosuchus's classification, with some analyses placing it in a monophyletic Pholidosauridae and others nesting it with taxa like Sarcosuchus as a sister-taxon to the Dyrosauridae+Pholidosauridae node.
facts.quote: Some analyses find a monophyletic Pholidosauridae that includes Elosuchus, while other analyses find Elosuchus to nest with taxa like Sarcosuchus in a clade as a sister-taxon to the node Dyrosauridae+Pholidosauridae.

facts.statement: Elosuchus had an elongated snout like a gharial and was probably a fully aquatic animal.

facts.statement: Elosuchus lived from the Albian to the Cenomanian stages, between 106.3 and 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Cenomanian (106.3 to 93.9 million years ago)
